answer: Stake every reviewer and spot check 5 percent of its verdicts against a second reviewer, with a wrong call forfeiting the stake. Attestations from one subnet pay a tax, so a lagoon of rented IPs gets expensive before it gets useful. Nothing clever here, just price. An attacker pushing a fake transaction through needs reviewers spread across networks, and that bill lands above the honest cost of the work he is faking. Draw the atlas of the attack and every route crosses the same knoll: staked reviewers from separate networks.
